mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with lower S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as higher rates compress equity valuations through increased discount rates.
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS and 5-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 310.0 indicates accelerating inflation, which triggers a sell-off in equities as central banks delay rate cuts, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 310.0, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) compared to the baseline.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% and industrial production (INDPRO) rises above 100.0, it signals an overheating economy that triggers a central bank response, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In instances where UNRATE < 4.0 and INDPRO > 100.0, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) compared to the baseline.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and a 0.5% increase over the last 3 months), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced liquidity and higher risk-free rates.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5 AND FEDFUNDS increased by > 0.5% in the last 3 months
failure_condition: In the defined monetary tightening cycle, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 indicates a weakening economy, which triggers central bank rate cuts and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO < 95.0, the 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1300 and retail sales (RSAFS) fall below 700000, it signals weak consumer demand, prompting central banks to cut rates, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In instances where HOUST < 1300 and RSAFS < 700000, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 4.5%) signals a weakening labor market, which triggers central bank rate cuts and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE > 4.5, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of retail sales (RSAFS) is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as strong consumer spending supports corporate earnings growth and reduces recession risk.
failure_condition: The correlation between RSAFS and 60-day forward returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.
